details: A recent survey by the European Central Bank (ECB) indicates that cryptocurrency payments remain marginal in the Eurozone. As of 2026, only 0.2% of online merchants and less than 1% of physical point-of-sale terminals accept crypto assets. This adoption rate shows minimal change from 2024, in stark contrast to mobile payments, which saw acceptance rise from 36% to 68% in the same period, while cash remained dominant at 92%. The primary reason cited for low crypto acceptance is consumer preference.
title: ECB Report: Crypto Payments Lag Significantly in Eurozone Adoption

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has once again reduced its forecast for global economic growth in 2026 to 3%. The revised outlook, detailed in its July World Economic Outlook update, attributes the slowdown to the persistent impact of the Middle East energy shock and the dynamics of a technology-driven investment boom. Concurrently, the IMF has increased its global inflation forecast for 2026 to 4.7%.
title: IMF Lowers 2026 Global Growth Forecast Amid Geopolitical and Tech Shifts

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has announced its intention to enable blockchain-based (Distributed Ledger Technology - DLT) transactions to settle in central bank money starting in 2026. This move is part of an effort to integrate DLT into Europe's existing monetary infrastructure and prevent fragmentation within tokenized markets. The announcement comes as discussions around the privacy implications of the proposed digital euro continue.
title: ECB Confirms DLT Transactions in Central Bank Money for 2026

details: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has ceased processing transactions involving 16 crypto platforms. This decision follows recent regulatory developments, with Binance warning users that attempted transfers after specified deadlines may undergo compliance reviews and lead to temporary restrictions on affected wallets. The move aligns with US and UK sanctions targeting specific Iranian and Russian crypto networks.
title: Binance Halts Transactions with 16 Platforms Amid Regulatory Scrutiny
